[SERIOUS] If you have to make a world a better place but can only do so by breaking a law in a significant way (but are allowed to get away with it), which laws would you break?

I've already done this before, and been convicted because of it (but not for it), but the details of that conviction are rather interesting. Basically a bunch of people were outraged at the inhumane and unethical behaviors of various legal groups representing copyright, and went on to show those unethical behaviors in light of day as well as protest the current status quo of copyright.

Later another group targeted credit card companies (avenge Assange). I was punished for this second, unrelated group, I had no activity or knowledge of. The courts did not accept them as different groups, in spite of the fact law defines a conspiracy as having one manifesto (our manifesto's were manifestly different). Therefore, according to ruling, I "conspired" with persons I never met, knew of, agreed with, or had any dealings with even by proxy. I was indicted for this second group because a jury will indict a ham sandwich, and indictments have no defense counsel to remind the jury that "Group X is not group Y". Therefore prosecutors spin any narrative they desire.

Due to abject poverty I signed a plea bargain against all ethics I stand for, as my defense counsel unanimously agreed it was "better" to do so. Setting a very dangerous precedent whereby persons of two dissimilar groups are now legally one group as long as prosecutors say so. At no point in my trial was the unrelated nature of these two groups raised as an important issue, because the issue was decided in the indictment (where I had no defense).

Did it make society better? Well, it has since halted the profit-seeking nature of various copyright organizations like mass mailings. It contributed to the knowledge that we, the society subject to these laws, do not agree with them and want them changed. It helped create some media awareness where before there was none, and helped prevent poor people from paying money they could not afford to pay when targeted by automated copyright threats.

Did the second group, which targeted financial institutions, make society better? Not in the least. Which is why I disagree with the idea, never participated, and now have no faith in society or law for punishing me for what I did not do. Were I tried for what I did, that is one matter. Being prosecuted and convicted for what you did not do...you don't recover.

I regret how it was done in the sense that it was done by a group of persons whose cultural behaviors are anathema to regular society. Which means it was incredibly easy to demonize us and twist anything done in favor of any prosecution. I also regret that I was forced into a plea bargain by the fact being arrested made me homeless, tripled the rent I had to pay, and ruined my health. I regret that now I need to word everything I discuss online as though I am being watched for, in all probability, the U.S. government is treating all such activities showing displeasure with authority as terrorism. I also regret that the government went to such extreme lengths to make actions, which were not illegal initially, a federal crime via legal precedent weaseling.

I know your question was hypothetical, but have a real reply to understand how reality really works. You are not given justice. You are not given choices. Prosecutors have all the power, juries indict ham sandwiches, and defense counsel will unanimously agree to plea bargain. You are given no resources, and resources you could have the prosecution can use against you (I could not get help from sympathetic groups for fear it'd be an additional claim that I was still "conspiring"). You also receive no certainty that you improved anything at all.

Edit: I am also wary of discussing it as I cannot afford legal counsel, and therefore have no means by which to determine whether anything I say is against some legal protection or court seal. For I also do not know of any such seals, but if they do exist I am culpable for breaking them. Therefore I must carefully stick to media released information until such a time as I can afford such legal counsel - which is definitely an ideal stranglehold "gag order" scenario the government would like.
